mainTopic: Using מעשר שני money for offerings: תודה loaves, designating the money for שלמים, and the rule that obligatory offerings come only from חולין
overview: The amud opens by finishing a debate about whether the loaves of a תודה may be made from wheat bought with מעשר שני money. The answer is no: the תודה is learned from שלמים, and שלמים are not the same kind of thing as מעשר, while wheat is. Next, רבי אמי rules that מעשר שני money designated for שלמים does not become שלמים. A challenge from a משנה about the hide of an animal bought with מעשר money is answered by רב and רבה. Then רבי יוחנן and רבי אלעזר disagree on the same question. The גמרא explains that their dispute depends on whether מעשר belongs to its owner (רבי יהודה) or to Heaven (רבי מאיר). A new משנה teaches that any obligatory offering, including a vowed תודה or שלמים, must come from חולין, learned from the פסח. The גמרא brings רבי אליעזר's proof that פסח itself comes from חולין, based on the פסח in מצרים. רבי עקיבא challenges that proof twice, and his second argument continues on the next amud.

steps.title: If peace offerings are not tithe themselves, the wheat should be allowed
steps.stepSummary: The challenger argues that since שלמים are learned from מעשר but are not themselves מעשר, the same should hold for the תודה. Wheat bought with מעשר שני money is not itself מעשר, so it should be allowed for the תודה loaves.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learn that שלמים may be bought with מעשר שני money from the word 'there' that appears both by שלמים and by מעשר. So, just as the שלמים are not themselves מעשר, the תודה is also not itself מעשר. And this wheat bought with מעשר שני money is also not itself מעשר, so why not use it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues a challenge that started earlier. The questioner uses the chain תודה → שלמים → מעשר to argue that wheat bought with מעשר שני money should be fine for the תודה loaves.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תודה is learned from שלמים, and שלמים are linked to מעשר through a גזירה שוה on the word 'there'. The questioner reads the lesson as: the offering itself is never actual מעשר produce, only something bought with its money. Wheat bought with מעשר money is in the same position, so it should be permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: A teaching learned from the same word appearing in two places in the Torah
Peace offerings
Thanks offering, brought together with loaves of bread
Second tithe, eaten in ירושלים or redeemed for money that is spent there
Their very selves, the thing itself

phrases.english: And peace offerings are learned through "there" and "there" from tithe.
phrases.notes: The word 'there' appears by שלמים (דברים 27:7) and by מעשר (דברים 14:23), so the two are linked.

phrases.english: And from this we can conclude:
Just as peace offerings are not themselves tithe,

phrases.aramaic: אַף תּוֹדָה נָמֵי אֵין גּוּפָהּ מַעֲשֵׂר,
phrases.english: so too a thanks offering is also not itself tithe,

phrases.aramaic: וְהָנֵי חִיטֵּי הַלְּקוּחוֹת בִּמְעוֹת מַעֲשֵׂר שֵׁנִי
phrases.english: and this wheat that is bought with second-tithe money
is also not itself tithe.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִינַּהּ: מָה שְׁלָמִים אֵין גּוּפָן מַעֲשֵׂר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues a challenge begun before this section against the rule that תודה loaves may not come from wheat bought with מעשר שני money.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that one may not make the תודה loaves from wheat bought with מעשר שני money
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The source that links the תודה to מעשר only teaches that the offering is not itself מעשר. Bought wheat is not itself מעשר either, so it should be allowed.

steps.title: The comparison is about species, and wheat is the species of tithe
steps.stepSummary: The responder explains that the lesson from שלמים is about kind, not status. שלמים are not the same species as מעשר, so the תודה loaves may not be the same species as מעשר, and wheat is.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let me tell you my reasoning. Where do I learn the תודה from? From שלמים. And שלמים are learned from מעשר through 'there' and 'there'. Just as שלמים are not the kind of thing that מעשר is, so too the תודה may not be the kind of thing that מעשר is. This rules out wheat bought with מעשר שני money, because wheat is the kind of thing that מעשר is.
steps.whatsHappening: The responder answers the challenge by explaining his own reasoning. The lesson from שלמים is about what kind of thing the offering is, and wheat is the same kind of food as מעשר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The responder keeps the same chain of learning (תודה → שלמים → מעשר) but reads the comparison differently. The questioner focused on status: the offering is not itself מעשר. The responder focuses on species: שלמים are animals, while מעשר is grain, wine and oil. Wheat bought with מעשר money is grain, the same species as מעשר, so it is excluded.

keyTerms.meaning: Let me say my own reasoning
The same kind or species as tithe produce
To exclude, to rule out

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up 'אין גופן מעשר' (not itself tithe) with 'אין מין מעשר' (not the same kind as tithe). The whole answer hangs on this switch: wheat bought with tithe money is not tithe itself, but it is the same kind of food as tithe.
steps.whatToRemember: The תודה loaves may not come from wheat bought with מעשר שני money, because the comparison to שלמים teaches that the offering must not be the same species as מעשר.

phrases.english: Let me say my reasoning:
A thanks offering, from where do I derive it?
From peace offerings,
and peace offerings are learned through "there" and "there" from tithe.
Just as peace offerings are not the species of tithe,
so too a thanks offering may not be the species of tithe,

phrases.aramaic: לְאַפּוֹקֵי חִיטִּין הַלְּקוּחוֹת בִּמְעוֹת מַעֲשֵׂר שֵׁנִי,
phrases.english: to exclude wheat bought with second-tithe money,
since it is the species of tithe.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 1 by reading the same source in a different way.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation of the comparison: from 'not itself tithe' to 'not the species of tithe'
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The comparison to שלמים only requires that the offering not be actual מעשר, so bought wheat would be allowed.
steps.terutzMaskana: The comparison requires that the offering not be the same species as מעשר, so wheat bought with מעשר money is excluded.

steps.title: Second-tithe money designated for a peace offering does not become a peace offering
steps.stepSummary: רבי אמי rules that designating מעשר שני money for שלמים does not give it the status of שלמים, because the קדושה of שלמים cannot take effect on top of the קדושה of מעשר שני.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אמי said: If someone designates מעשר שני money for a שלמים, it does not become שלמים. Why not? Because the holiness of שלמים is not strong enough to take hold on top of the holiness of מעשר שני.
steps.whatsHappening: A new statement opens a new topic. רבי אמי gives a rule about trying to put the holiness of a שלמים directly onto מעשר שני money.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally you buy a שלמים with מעשר שני money, but here the person tries to declare the money itself as שלמים. רבי אמי says this does not work. The money already has the קדושה of מעשר שני, and the קדושה of שלמים is not strong enough to rest on something that is already holy in that way.

keyTerms.meaning: One who designates or attaches holiness to an item by declaration
They did not acquire, meaning they did not take on the status
Strong, powerful
To take effect, to rest upon
Holiness, sanctity

steps.whyThisMatters: It sets up a principle about one kind of holiness resting on another, which the גמרא immediately tests with a משנה.

phrases.english: Rabbi Ami says:
One who designates second-tithe money for a peace offering,
the money does not take on the status of a peace offering.
What is the reason?
Because the sanctity of a peace offering is not strong enough
to take effect on the sanctity of second tithe.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אַמֵּי: הַמַּתְפִּיס מְעוֹת מַעֲשֵׂר שֵׁנִי לִשְׁלָמִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new, related topic about מעשר שני money and שלמים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Designating מעשר שני money as שלמים does not work, because the קדושה of שלמים cannot rest on the קדושה of מעשר שני.

steps.title: Challenge from the hide of an animal bought with tithe money
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי אמי from a משנה. Someone who misused מעשר שני money to buy a wild animal for שלמים, or a domestic animal for ordinary meat, is told that the hide does not become חולין. This seems to show that it takes on the status of שלמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: We have a challenge: Someone who buys a wild animal for שלמים, or a domestic animal for ordinary meat, with מעשר שני money: the hide does not become חולין. Doesn't this mean it does become שלמים?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a משנה that seems to contradict רבי אמי. The step ends with a question that sharpens the contradiction, and the next step answers it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally, when you buy a שלמים with מעשר money, the hide is חולין. Here, in cases of misuse, the hide does not become חולין. The גמרא suggests this means the שלמים status did take effect through מעשר שני money, which goes against רבי אמי's claim that it cannot.

keyTerms.meaning: A wild animal, which cannot be brought as a קרבן
A domestic animal
Ordinary meat eaten for enjoyment, not as a קרבן
Non-sacred, ordinary
Is this not to say? Used to draw an implication from a source

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
One who buys an undomesticated animal for peace offerings,
phrases.notes: He bought it with מעשר שני money, and a wild animal can't be a קרבן at all.

phrases.english: or a domesticated animal for ordinary meat,
the hide does not become non-sacred.
Is that not to say that it takes on the status of a peace offering?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי אמי's ruling from step 3 using a משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אמי's rule that מעשר שני money cannot take on the status of שלמים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה says the hide does not become חולין in these cases, which suggests the שלמים status did take effect through מעשר שני money, against רבי אמי.

steps.title: רב explains the משנה: the hide never became שלמים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers the challenge from the משנה. רב already said the animal does not become שלמים. The phrase 'the hide does not go out to חולין' means this case is simply not in the category where the hide goes out to חולין.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it was already said about that משנה that רב ruled: it does not become שלמים. So what does 'the hide does not go out to חולין' mean? This is what it means: this animal is not in the category of a hide that goes out to חולין.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבי אמי by showing the משנה from step 4 never meant the animal became שלמים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 4 read 'the hide does not become חולין' as proof that the animal had שלמים status. רב reads it differently: the special rule where the hide goes out to חולין belongs to a real שלמים, and this animal never was one. So the משנה does not contradict רבי אמי.

keyTerms.meaning: Does not take on (the status); the designation does not take effect
Ordinary, non-holy property
This is what it means (a rereading of a source)
In the category of, under the rules of

steps.confusionAlert: 'The hide does not go out to חולין' does not mean the hide stays holy as שלמים. It means the usual rule about the hide simply does not apply here, because this was never a real שלמים.

phrases.english: Wasn't it stated about it,
phrases.notes: 'It' is the משנה quoted in the challenge, the one about the wild animal bought with מעשר שני money.

phrases.english: Rav said: it does not take on the status of שלמים,
and what is meant by 'the hide does not go out to non-holy status'?
This is what it is saying:
it is not in the category where the hide goes out to non-holy status,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 4 against רבי אמי.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the wording of the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה meant the animal became שלמים, so the hide could not become חולין.
steps.terutzMaskana: The animal never became שלמים. The משנה only says the special hide rule does not apply to it.

steps.title: Why doesn't the animal become anything holy?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason behind רב's explanation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why this purchase does not give the animal a holy status. It is setting up רבה's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב said the animal is not שלמים, but he did not explain why. The question asks what makes this purchase different from a proper purchase with מעשר שני money.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind רב's reading in step 5.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the animal bought improperly with מעשר שני money does not take on a holy status.

steps.title: רבה: like buying an ox for plowing
steps.stepSummary: רבה explains that using the מעשר שני money improperly is treated like buying an ox for plowing, a purchase that does not carry the holiness of מעשר שני.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: he is treated as if he bought an ox for plowing.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה answers the question. Because the money was used the wrong way, the animal is treated like an ox bought for farm work, which has no holy status.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מעשר שני money may only be spent on food to eat in ירושלים. Buying an ox to plow with is a misuse, so no holiness passes to the ox. In the same way, a wild animal cannot be a שלמים, so buying one 'for שלמים' is a misuse and the animal gets no holy status.

keyTerms.meaning: An ox for plowing, a non-food purchase
He is treated like...

steps.whatToRemember: רבי אמי's rule stands: the משנה about the hide does not prove that שלמים status takes effect on מעשר שני money.

phrases.english: Rabba said:
He is treated like one who buys an ox for plowing.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה: נַעֲשָׂה כְּלוֹקֵחַ שׁוֹר לַחֲרִישָׁה
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The improper purchase is treated like buying an ox for plowing, so the animal has no holy status.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן and רבי אלעזר disagree
steps.stepSummary: A dispute is brought about designating מעשר שני money for שלמים. רבי יוחנן says it takes effect, and רבי אלעזר says it does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: if someone designates מעשר שני money for שלמים, רבי יוחנן says it takes on that status, and רבי אלעזר says it does not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new section with a dispute between two אמוראים on the same question רבי אמי ruled on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר reaches the same ruling as רבי אמי: the designation does not work. רבי יוחנן disagrees and says it does. The next steps explain what each side's view depends on.

keyTerms.meaning: One who designates something (here money) for a holy purpose
It takes on (the status); the designation takes effect
Second tithe, eaten in ירושלים or redeemed for money

phrases.english: It was stated:
One who designates second-tithe money for a peace offering:
Rabbi Yochanan says: it takes on the status,
Rabbi Elazar says: it does not take on the status.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיתְּמַר, הַמַּתְפִּיס מְעוֹת מַעֲשֵׂר שֵׁנִי לִשְׁלָמִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a dispute on the same question as רבי אמי's ruling in step 3.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוחנן: designating מעשר שני money for שלמים takes effect. רבי אלעזר: it does not.

steps.title: The dispute exists only according to רבי מאיר
steps.stepSummary: According to רבי יהודה, who holds that מעשר is a person's private property, everyone agrees the designation works. The dispute is only according to רבי מאיר, who holds that מעשר is Heaven's property.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to רבי יהודה, who says מעשר is the property of an ordinary person, everyone agrees it takes effect. They disagree according to רבי מאיר, who says מעשר is the property of the Most High.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא narrows the dispute and shows which view of מעשר it depends on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If מעשר belongs to the owner (רבי יהודה), he can designate his own money for שלמים like any other money. If מעשר belongs to Heaven (רבי מאיר), we must ask whether a person can designate money that is not his.

keyTerms.meaning: Property of an ordinary person
Property of the Most High, belonging to Heaven
Everyone agrees
According to the view of...

phrases.english: And according to Rabbi Yehuda, who said:
tithe is the property of an ordinary person –
everyone agrees that it takes on the status.

phrases.aramaic: כִּי פְּלִיגִי אַלִּיבָּא דְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר, דְּאָמַר:
phrases.english: Where they disagree is according to Rabbi Meir, who said:
tithe is the property of the Most High.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַלִּיבָּא דְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה, דְּאָמַר: מַעֲשֵׂר מָמוֹן הֶדְיוֹט הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defines the scope of the dispute in step 8.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יהודה, all agree it takes effect. The dispute is only according to רבי מאיר.

steps.title: The reasoning of each side
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר follows רבי מאיר, so Heaven's money cannot be designated. רבי יוחנן says that since מעשר itself is brought as שלמים, designating it for שלמים also works.
steps.simpleTranslation: The one who says it does not take effect follows רבי מאיר. The one who says it does take effect reasons: since מעשר is brought as שלמים, when he designates it for שלמים, the designation also takes hold.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why each אמורא holds as he does, both working within רבי מאיר's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר: money that belongs to Heaven cannot be given a new holy status. רבי יוחנן: an animal bought with מעשר money is normally offered as שלמים anyway, so מעשר and שלמים fit together, and designating the money for שלמים works even according to רבי מאיר.

keyTerms.meaning: Is brought (as an offering)
Takes hold; the designation takes effect

phrases.aramaic: מַאן דְּאָמַר לָא קָנֵי – כְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר,
phrases.english: The one who says it does not take on the status – holds like Rabbi Meir,
and the one who says it takes on the status –
since tithe is brought as a peace offering,
phrases.notes: Some versions read קרי, 'is called' a peace offering. The corrected wording, in square brackets, is קריב, 'is brought' as one.

phrases.english: when you designate it, the designation also takes hold.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאן דְּאָמַר לָא קָנֵי – כְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives each side's reason within רבי מאיר's view from step 9.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אלעזר: Heaven's money cannot be designated. רבי יוחנן: since מעשר is brought as שלמים, the designation takes hold.

steps.title: A ברייתא requires two fifths when redeeming
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says that if מעשר שני money was designated for שלמים, its redemption needs two added fifths, one for the offering's holiness and one for the מעשר. This shows the שלמים status did take effect, against רבי אלעזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged from a ברייתא: one who designates מעשר שני money for שלמים, when he redeems it, adds two fifths, one for the holy offering and one for the מעשר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי אלעזר with a ברייתא that seems to show the designation did take effect.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Redeeming something holy usually requires adding a fifth. Two fifths are required here, so the money must hold two holy statuses at once: מעשר and שלמים. That suggests the שלמים status took hold, against רבי אלעזר.

keyTerms.meaning: He redeems them (exchanges their holiness onto other money)
Fifths added as an extra payment when redeeming
Property given to the Temple; here, the holiness of the offering

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
One who designates second-tithe money for a peace offering,
when he redeems it –
he adds to it two fifths,
one for the consecrated status and one for the tithe.

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵיתִיבִי: הַמַּתְפִּיס מְעוֹת מַעֲשֵׂר שֵׁנִי לִשְׁלָמִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי אלעזר's position from step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אלעזר, who says designating מעשר שני money for שלמים does not take effect.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Two fifths are added, so the money carries both מעשר holiness and שלמים holiness. That means the designation took effect.

steps.title: The ברייתא follows רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers the challenge to רבי אלעזר. The ברייתא that requires two added fifths follows רבי יהודה, who holds that מעשר is a person's own property.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do you think that ברייתא is everyone's opinion? Whose opinion is it? It is רבי יהודה's.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבי אלעזר by saying the ברייתא only reflects רבי יהודה's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 9 we learned that, according to רבי יהודה, everyone agrees that designating the money for שלמים works. So the ברייתא is no problem for רבי אלעזר, who follows רבי מאיר, under whose view Heaven's money cannot be designated.

keyTerms.meaning: Everyone's opinion; a ruling with no dispute
Whose opinion is this? (asking which sage a source follows)

steps.whatToRemember: The challenge to רבי אלעזר is answered: the ברייתא follows רבי יהודה, while רבי אלעזר follows רבי מאיר.

phrases.english: Do you think it is the opinion of everyone?
phrases.notes: He means the ברייתא from the last step, the one that requires two added fifths.

phrases.english: Whose opinion is this? It is רבי יהודה's.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי סָבְרַתְּ דִּבְרֵי הַכֹּל הִיא? הָא מַנִּי?
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigning the source to one side of a dispute (it is not unanimous)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא is everyone's view, so it refutes רבי אלעזר
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא follows רבי יהודה, who holds מעשר is private property. רבי אלעזר follows רבי מאיר.

steps.title: Obligatory offerings must come from חולין, learned from פסח
steps.stepSummary: The משנה asks how we know a vowed תודה must be bought only with חולין money. It learns this from the פסוק of פסח that says 'צאן ובקר'.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know that someone who says 'I take upon myself a תודה' may bring it only from חולין? The פסוק says: 'You shall slaughter the פסח to ה׳ your God, צאן ובקר.' But פסח comes only from sheep and goats. So why does it say 'צאן ובקר'? To compare everything that comes from the flock and the herd to פסח. Just as פסח is an obligation and comes only from חולין, so too every obligation comes only from חולין.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It teaches a general rule: any offering brought as an obligation must be paid for with חולין money.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק mentions 'בקר' (cattle), but a פסח can never be cattle, so the extra word must teach something. It links all animal offerings to פסח. Like פסח, any obligatory offering must come from חולין and not from מעשר שני money.

keyTerms.meaning: A thanks offering
Ordinary, non-sacred money or property
A Torah comparison that links two topics so they share laws
Something a person is obligated to bring
Flock (sheep and goats) and herd (cattle)

steps.confusionAlert: The פסוק says 'צאן ובקר', but a פסח cannot be brought from cattle. The משנה itself points this out, and that is exactly why it reads the words as a comparison.

phrases.english: משנה
From where do we know, for one who says: "It is upon me to bring a thanks offering,"
that he may bring it only from non-sacred money?
The verse states: "And you shall slaughter the Pesach to ה׳ your God,
flock and herd."
But doesn't the Pesach come
only from sheep and from goats?

phrases.aramaic: אִם כֵּן מָה תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר ״צֹאן וּבָקָר״?
phrases.english: If so, why does the verse say "flock and herd"?

phrases.aramaic: לְהַקִּישׁ כׇּל הַבָּא מִן הַצֹּאן וּמִן הַבָּקָר לְפֶסַח:
phrases.english: To compare everything that comes from the flock and the herd to the Pesach:
Just as the Pesach is a matter of obligation
and comes only from non-sacred money,
so too every matter of obligation
comes only from non-sacred money.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה on a new rule
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Every obligatory offering must be bought with חולין, learned through a הקש to פסח from the words 'צאן ובקר'.

steps.title: Applying the rule to vowed תודה, שלמים, and נסכים
steps.stepSummary: Because of the rule, a vowed תודה or שלמים must come from חולין. נסכים must always come from חולין.
steps.simpleTranslation: Therefore, someone who says 'I take upon myself a תודה' or 'I take upon myself שלמים' must bring them only from חולין, since they now come as an obligation. And נסכים, in every case, come only from חולין.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה applies the rule from the previous step to specific cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once a person says 'הרי עלי', he has made a vow, so the offering becomes an obligation he owes. That makes it fall under the rule of 'דבר שבחובה'. נסכים are stricter: they must always come from חולין, even with no vow.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It is upon me' — the wording of a vow that creates an obligation
Peace offerings
Wine (and flour and oil) offerings brought with a sacrifice
In every case, no matter what

steps.confusionAlert: A vowed offering sounds voluntary, but once the vow is made it becomes an obligation. That is why it must come from חולין.

phrases.english: Therefore, one who says: "It is upon me to bring a thanks offering,"
or "It is upon me to bring a peace offering,"
since they come as an obligation,
they may be brought only from non-sacred money.
And libations, in every case,
may be brought only from non-sacred money.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the general rule of step 13 to specific cases
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A vowed תודה or שלמים must come from חולין, and נסכים must always come from חולין.

steps.title: How do we know פסח itself comes from חולין?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source that פסח itself must be brought from חולין.
steps.simpleTranslation: And פסח itself, from where do we know it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins and asks a basic question. The משנה built everything on פסח, so where do we learn that פסח must come from חולין? This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה's comparison only works if we already know that פסח must come from חולין. The משנה assumed this without giving a source, so the גמרא looks for one.

keyTerms.meaning: Itself
From where do we know this?

phrases.english: גמרא
And the Pesach itself, from where do we know it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source behind the משנה's basic assumption
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source that פסח must be bought with חולין

steps.title: The פסח in מצרים teaches the פסח for later generations
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר compares the פסח brought in מצרים to the פסח of later generations. Just as the first came only from חולין, so must the later ones.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: רבי אליעזר says, 'פסח' is said about מצרים, and 'פסח' is said about later generations. Just as the פסח in מצרים came only from חולין, so too the פסח for the generations comes only from חולין.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a ברייתא. It links the first פסח, in מצרים, to every later פסח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same word, 'פסח', is used for both, so they share their laws. The פסח in מצרים came only from חולין, since there was no מעשר שני there yet. So every later פסח must also come only from חולין.

keyTerms.meaning: The first פסח offering, brought in מצרים
The פסח offering brought every year in later generations

steps.whatToRemember: The chain: פסח מצרים came from חולין, so פסח דורות must too, and through the הקש of 'צאן ובקר', so must every obligatory offering.

phrases.english: As it was taught in a ברייתא: רבי אליעזר says:
"Pesach" is said about Egypt,
and "Pesach" is said about later generations.
Just as the Pesach mentioned regarding Egypt
came only from non-sacred property,
so too the Pesach mentioned for the generations
comes only from non-sacred property.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר: נֶאֱמַר פֶּסַח בְּמִצְרַיִם
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A comparison between פסח מצרים, which came only from חולין, and פסח דורות

steps.title: רבי עקיבא: You can't learn a choice from a case with no choice
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא challenges רבי אליעזר's proof. In מצרים there was no מעשר שני money at all, so of course the פסח came from חולין. You cannot learn from that to later times, when there is a real option.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא said to him: Can we learn a case where something is possible from a case where it was impossible?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא attacks the proof that רבי אליעזר just brought from the פסח in מצרים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In מצרים there was no מעשר שני yet, so bringing the פסח from מעשר money was impossible. Today it is possible. So the fact that the first פסח came from חולין shows nothing about what is allowed when there is a real choice.

keyTerms.meaning: We learn or derive (one law from another case)
Possible; a situation where there is a real choice
Impossible; a situation where there was no other option

steps.confusionAlert: רבי עקיבא is not saying the פסח in מצרים came from מעשר money. He agrees it came from חולין. He says this happened only because there was no other option.

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva said to him:
phrases.notes: "Him" is רבי אליעזר, who just brought the proof from the פסח in מצרים.

phrases.english: But do we derive the possible from the impossible?
phrases.notes: In מצרים there was no מעשר שני money to use. Later there is, so the two cases are not the same.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the comparison רבי אליעזר made in Step 16.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אליעזר's comparison between the פסח in מצרים and the פסח of later generations.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The first case had no alternative, so it cannot teach a rule for a case where an alternative exists.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר: It is still a strong proof
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר holds his ground. Even though using other money was impossible in מצרים, the פסח there is still a great proof, and we learn from it.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Even though it was impossible, it is a great proof, and we will learn from it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר answers רבי עקיבא's challenge and keeps his proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר admits the facts: in מצרים there was no choice. He still holds that the first פסח sets the model for every later פסח. So the source of its money is a real rule and not just an accident of the time.

keyTerms.meaning: A great (strong) proof
And we will learn (the rule) from it

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאִי אֶפְשָׁר,
phrases.english: He said to him: Even though it was impossible,
phrases.notes: Now רבי אליעזר is the one answering רבי עקיבא.

phrases.english: it is a great proof, and we will learn from it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאִי אֶפְשָׁר, רְאָיָיה גְּדוֹלָה הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defends Step 16 against the challenge in Step 17.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rejects the challenge and keeps the original proof.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי עקיבא thought a case with no choice cannot teach a rule.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי אליעזר holds that the first פסח is a strong model even though there was no choice then.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא's second attack: the Egypt פסח was different
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא tries another argument. The פסח in מצרים was a weaker kind of offering. Its blood was not placed on the מזבח, and its parts were not burned on the מזבח. So it cannot teach about later פסחים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא came back and argued another way: What about the פסח of מצרים? It is different, because it did not need its blood placed, or its sacrificial parts brought, on the מזבח.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא starts a new challenge, showing a difference between the פסח in מצרים and later ones. He is setting up his argument, and it continues in the next lines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a new kind of attack. Before, רבי עקיבא said there was no choice. Now he points to a real difference in the offering itself. The פסח in מצרים had no מזבח service for blood or אימורין, so it was a lighter offering. A stricter offering might be different.

keyTerms.meaning: Another line of reasoning
The פסח offering brought in מצרים before the Exodus
Placing the blood of an offering on the מזבח
The parts of an offering that are burned on the מזבח

phrases.aramaic: חָזַר רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא וְדָנוֹ דִּין אַחֵר:
phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva then reasoned it another way:
What about the Paschal offering of Egypt?
For it did not require placement of blood
or sacrificial portions on the altar,

steps.triggerLanguage: חָזַר רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא וְדָנוֹ דִּין אַחֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After Step 18 rejected his first challenge, רבי עקיבא opens a new challenge to the same proof.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אליעזר's comparison of the פסח in מצרים to the פסח of later generations.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסח in מצרים had no blood placement or אימורין on the מזבח. Because it was a lighter offering, it cannot set the rule for the later פסח.
